what: review M5: a panel left open and unlooked-at (a stream viewer acking frames on https://example.com/, nothing else), sampled every 5 minutes
reading: The Workspace browser's Browser Run session was up at 5 and 10 minutes (age 600 s) and gone from the Environment's record by 15: an idle page repaints nothing, so a viewer causes no CDP traffic, and Browser Run's 10-minute keep-alive ended the session; the Shadow's `disconnected` handler removed it. So a hidden panel on an idle page holds a browser for at most about 10 to 15 minutes, not 30: browser-seconds for this run at most 900 (about $0.02 past the free hours). A page that keeps repainting (an animation) sends frames and would hold it while the viewer stays. The harness's own 20-minute guard cut the run at minute 20, so this file is written from its log; Browser Run's close reason was not read.
